s1: Service desk (L1) is provided by the client and is out of scope for this team.

s1.title: Single point of failure on a shift
s1.note: With one person per tier on a shift, sickness or attrition leaves the shift uncovered. Mitigation: named cross-trained backup on call.

s1.title: Handover loss between locations
s1.note: Context is lost at follow-the-sun handovers and resolution slows. Mitigation: handover runbook and a 30-minute overlap.

s1.title: Attrition and backfill lag
s1.note: Replacements take 6–10 weeks to hire and ramp. Mitigation: shadow resource in the offshore bench.

s1.title: Coverage window grows after signature
s1.note: Client asks for weekend or extended hours later. Tracked only: priced as a change request in the SOW, no FTE added.

s2.title: No volumetrics for some towers
s2.note: Demand comes from a complexity or MAU proxy, not ticket history. Mitigation: volume band clause in the SOW and a request for 3–6 months of tickets ([F] Sc.1).

s2.title: Undiscovered integrations and dependencies
s2.note: Hidden interfaces raise L3 effort after takeover. Mitigation: portfolio analysis as a pre-proposal investment ([F] Sc.1 risk log).

s2.title: Niche skill availability
s2.note: Special or legacy skills are hard to hire in the chosen locations. Mitigation: named bench or partner capacity.

s2.title: Work team below the coverage floor
s2.note: If the work needs fewer people than the shifts, the team is lifted to the base team and has spare time. Tracked only: use it for transformation or enhancements.

s3.title: Skills needed live outside the chosen shifts
s3.note: P1 incidents out of hours may need the specialist hands-on, not just reachable. Mitigation: on-call response SLA and escalation path in the SOW.

s3.title: On-call rota too thin
s3.note: One specialist cannot carry a sustainable on-call rota. Tracked only: at least two people share each on-call rota.

s3.title: Shift pattern changes after transition
s3.note: The client moves core hours or adds a region, so live shifts move. Mitigation: shift changes handled as a change request.

s4.title: AI tool integration complexity
s4.note: Client tooling needs more work to integrate than planned. Mitigation: 2-week technical spike during transition ([F] Sc.2 risk log).

s4.title: AI roadmap slippage
s4.note: Use cases land later than planned. Tracked only: PoC-gated commitments and no AI savings committed in Y1 ([F] Sc.1 risk log).

s4.title: Incumbent AI lock-in
s4.note: Proprietary incumbent tooling can't be reused. Mitigation: tooling portability requirements in the SOW assumptions ([F] Sc.2 risk log).

s5.title: Heavy governance cadence
s5.note: Weekly exec reviews, monthly performance reviews, QBRs and CAB across several client stakeholder groups ([F] Sc.3 Step 4). Mitigation: agree the cadence in the SOW.

s5.title: Single SDM is a key-person dependency
s5.note: Tracked only: a named deputy from the delivery leads covers leave and escalation.

s6.title: Senior talent availability
s6.note: A senior-heavy pyramid needs more Leads and Seniors than the chosen locations may supply in time. Tracked only: confirm bench before signing.

s6.title: Client pushback on grade mix
s6.note: The client's rate card caps senior grades. Tracked only: agree the pyramid in the commercial assumptions.

s7.title: Volume growth beyond the baseline
s7.note: Ticket volume grows and eats the savings. Mitigation: volume band clause with a re-baseline trigger ([F] Sc.3 risk log).

s7.title: Savings depend on client access and tooling
s7.note: Tracked only: productivity gains are contingent on AI maturity assessment and client system access approval ([F] Sc.1).

s8.title: Existing team includes out-of-scope work
s8.note: Today's team may also do L1, projects or enhancements that are not in our scope. Check role by role before comparing.

s8.title: Hidden capacity in the existing team
s8.note: Client staff or shared incumbent teams quietly absorb L2/L3 work, so today's headcount understates the real effort ([F] Annexure 2: hidden work content).

s8.title: Existing team is over-staffed
s8.note: A large incumbent team reflects low automation, not the work. Use Stage 7 savings to show the path down.
